No fixed release tagged yet; reporter and maintainer describe all current versions as affected. Maintainer notes the risky registration timing dates to commit 1da1caed (Epiphany 45.x era); before that the handlers were always registered and similarly reachable from web content.

CVE-2026-117028.description: Skuul School Management System through version 2.6.5 is vulnerable to incorrect access control in the ResultChecker::checkResult method. An authenticated student can manipulate the studentId parameter to retrieve another student's examination results, including examination marks, without authorization.

CVE-2026-117350.description: Bitcoin Core prior to 29.5, 30.4, 31.2 and 32.1 is vulnerable to an OOM issue.

CVE-2026-118986.description: CallBackery versions before 0.62.0 for Perl allow session cookie forgery via a signing secret generated with rand(). The secret that signs session cookies is built from two calls to the built-in rand(), which is seeded with 32 bits. The secret therefore has at most 2**32 possible values, and one signed cookie is enough to test each candidate offline. An attacker who obtains a single session cookie can recover the secret and sign cookies for any user, including an administrator.

CVE-2026-118987.description: CallBackery versions before 0.62.0 for Perl accept session cookies of any age sent in the X-Session-Cookie header. cookieConf() rejects a cookie older than 300 seconds only when it arrives in the xsc query parameter. The same cookie sent in the X-Session-Cookie header is accepted however old it is. A session cookie that leaks through a log, a Referer header or browser history authenticates as its user indefinitely.

CVE-2026-119528.description: A flaw was found in GIMP. The PSD plug-in’s image resource header loader uses an incorrect destination size when copying a converted resource name into a fixed stack buffer. Opening a crafted PSD file can cause a stack-based buffer overflow, leading to a crash and potentially arbitrary code execution.

CVE-2026-119542.description: A flaw was found in the Ickle query parser in Infinispan. A query containing deeply nested predicates can cause recursive parsing to exhaust the Java thread stack and throw an uncaught StackOverflowError. An authenticated user with BULK_READ permission who can submit a cache query may trigger the issue, potentially affecting availability.

CVE-2026-119569.description: Parse Server before 8.6.108 and 9.0.0 before 9.10.5-alpha.9 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability because user-controlled keys are expanded into objects without own-property checks. Clients with class write access can send dot notation field keys or ACL entry names matching built-in object members to corrupt built-in functions, causing all requests to fail until server restart.

CVE-2026-119570.description: Parse Server from 9.7.0 before 9.10.5-alpha.7 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows clients to receive protected field values written by beforeSave triggers using dot notation keys. When protectedFieldsSaveResponseExempt is set to false, clients with create or update permission can read values a trigger writes beneath a protected field in the same request.

CVE-2026-119571.description: Parse Server from 9.7.0 before 9.10.5-alpha.10 contains an authorization flaw that applies _Installation updates addressed by object ID to the installation named in the X-Parse-Installation-Id header. When protectedFieldsTriggerExempt is enabled, attackers knowing another installation's object ID can make a beforeSave trigger process that installation's protected fields while writing elsewhere.

CVE-2026-119572.description: Traefik from 3.7.0-ea.1 before 3.7.15 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider that silently disables mTLS configured via the auth-tls-secret annotation. When another Ingress declares a path on the same host without matching auth-tls settings, Traefik falls back to default TLS options, letting unauthenticated attackers reach backends requiring client certificates.

CVE-2026-119573.description: Traefik 3.7.11 before 3.7.15 contains an authorization bypass in the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider that skips the cross-namespace check on the auth-tls-secret annotation when a cached client authentication TLS option is reused. Users who can create Ingresses can reference another namespace's CA secret already used by another Ingress, enforcing it on their own routes and learning whether it exists, without disclosure of its contents.

CVE-2026-119574.description: Traefik from 3.2.0 before 3.7.15 contains a data race in the experimental FastProxy that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the process by abusing HTTP/1 protocol upgrades. Attackers can repeatedly open and abort upgraded connections such as WebSocket, corrupting the unsynchronized shared bufio.Reader and triggering an unrecovered panic that terminates Traefik.

CVE-2026-119575.description: ArcadeDB from 26.8.1 before 26.10.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users with updateDatabaseSettings to disable the LOAD CSV IP block list via ALTER DATABASE. Attackers can set arcadedb.opencypher.loadCsv.blockedIpRanges to an empty string, then issue LOAD CSV requests to read cloud metadata and internal loopback or private services.

CVE-2026-119576.description: ArcadeDB from 21.12.1 before 26.10.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows users with only readRecord to replace the shared GraphQL schema via the read-only query endpoint. Attackers can send a GraphQL type definition with a crafted @sql directive to /api/v1/query/{database}, altering query results returned to other users including administrators.

CVE-2026-119577.description: ArcadeDB before 26.10.2 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows revoked users to retain access through already-open Postgres, Bolt, MongoDB, or Redis wire-protocol connections. Attackers holding an existing connection can keep reading and writing data after deletion, grant removal, or password rotation, because executors keep a stale ServerSecurityUser.

CVE-2026-119578.description: MONAI from 1.6.0 before 1.6.1 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in Auto3DSeg algo_from_json() that allows attackers to run Python code via a crafted work directory's algo_object.json. Attackers can ship a malicious algorithm_templates module plus a _target_ name that is imported and instantiated when victims call AutoRunner or import_bundle_algo_history, executing code under default configuration.

CVE-2026-119596.description: UNIT3D through 9.2.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in PlaylistZipController::show that allows authenticated users to download other members' private playlists. Attackers can enumerate sequential playlist ids at the /playlist-zips/{playlist} endpoint to obtain zips of all torrents, disclosing private collection membership.

CVE-2026-119597.description: OpenDeepWiki through 2.0.6 contains a hard-coded JWT signing key vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge administrator tokens using the publicly known Jwt:SecretKey in appsettings.json. Attackers can mint HS256 bearer tokens with an Admin role claim to access /api/admin endpoints and control users, roles, repositories, settings, and API keys.

CVE-2026-119598.description: Miaomiaowu before 0.9.3 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in /api/user/proxy-provider-configs that allows authenticated users to read other users' configurations. Attackers can iterate the global auto-increment external_subscription_id parameter to disclose override scripts, filter rules, custom request headers and health-check URLs.

CVE-2026-119599.description: AxonHub through 1.0.0-beta11 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows project users to assign system-level scopes by creating service_account API keys with unvalidated scopes. Attackers holding write_api_keys can mint keys with read_channels and query /admin/graphql to read every channel's configuration, including base URLs and model lists.

CVE-2026-119600.description: tcpflow through 1.6.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read process memory by sending packets with forged IP payload lengths. Attackers can inject crafted IPv4 or IPv6 TCP packets into captured traffic or pcap files to leak adjacent memory into reconstructed flow files or crash tcpflow.

CVE-2026-119601.description: AFFLIB through 3.7.22 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in af_get_page() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying crafted AFF images with mismatched page and sector sizes. Attackers can set a page size larger than and not a multiple of the sector size, causing the sector zero-fill loop to write past the buffer and crash forensic tools.

CVE-2026-119602.description: libmspack through 0.11alpha contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in the MS-ZIP decompressor that allows attackers to leak heap data via unchecked back-reference distances. Attackers can supply a crafted MS-ZIP CAB file whose first block begins with a back-reference, causing cabd->extract() to write up to 32 KiB of stale heap memory into extracted output.

CVE-2026-86715.description: Plaintext storage of a password vulnerability in Crypttech Crypto and Informatics Technologies Industry and Trade Inc. Vatos DLP allows Use of Known Domain Credentials. This issue affects Vatos DLP: from 1.1.176 before 1.1.243.

CVE-2026-91912.description: Dell OpenManage Enterprise, versions prior to 4.8.0, contains an Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Information disclosure.

CVE-2026-91913.description: Dell OpenManage Enterprise, versions prior to 4.8.0, contains an Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection') vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Command execution.

CVE-2026-91914.description: Dell OpenManage Enterprise, versions prior to 4.8.0, contains an Authentication Bypass by Spoofing vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with adjacent network access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Session theft.

CVE-2026-91915.description: Dell OpenManage Enterprise, versions prior to 4.8.0, contains an Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component ('Injection') vulnerability. A high privileged attacker with adjacent network access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Script injection.

9443006c98c0f965e062bdaf.title_ko: 삼성전자, 삼성디스플레이 보유 TCL CSOT 지분 전량 인수
9443006c98c0f965e062bdaf.summary_ko: 삼성전자가 자회사 삼성디스플레이가 보유한 중국 디스플레이 기업 TCL CSOT의 지분 10.16%를 약 1조 2718억 원에 전량 인수하기로 했습니다. 이는 LCD 사업에서 철수한 삼성디스플레이의 지분 정리와 더불어, 삼성전자의 LCD 패널 공급망 확보 및 전략적 협력 관계 강화를 위한 조치로 풀이됩니다.

4ed79bb48f9fa6aaeab12dc0.title_ko: 공식 Claude Code VS Code 확장 프로그램에서 SSH 백도어 악성코드 발견
4ed79bb48f9fa6aaeab12dc0.summary_ko: 공식 'Claude Code' VS Code 확장 프로그램이 악성코드에 감염되어 사용자 시스템에 SSH 백도어를 설치하는 사건이 발생했습니다. 공격자는 합법적인 확장 코드 앞에 악성 로더를 삽입해 사용자의 SSH 키를 탈취하고 지속적인 접근 통로를 구축했습니다. 최대 5,000명의 사용자가 피해를 입었을 것으로 추정되며, 해당 확장 프로그램을 사용한 이들은 즉시 관련 자격 증명을 갱신해야 합니다.

a61642ce2e28c48a7b7fa9cb.title_ko: TeamViewer 원격 제어 취약점, 원격 코드 실행 및 시스템 장악 가능
a61642ce2e28c48a7b7fa9cb.summary_ko: TeamViewer에서 정수 오버플로로 인한 고위험 취약점(CVE-2026-111585)이 발견되어 시스템 장악 및 코드 실행 위험이 확인되었습니다. 공격자는 조작된 호스트 화면 데이터를 통해 뷰어의 시스템을 제어하거나 충돌시킬 수 있습니다. TeamViewer는 버전 15.83 업데이트를 통해 해당 문제를 패치했으므로 사용자들은 즉시 보안 업데이트를 적용해야 합니다.

5e70503e7483ef2332bdedf1.title_ko: 바이낸스 8조 원대 해킹 배후에 북한 라자루스 지목
5e70503e7483ef2332bdedf1.summary_ko: 바이낸스에서 발생한 8조 4천억 원 규모의 암호화폐 탈취 사건의 배후로 북한 해킹 조직 '라자루스'가 지목되었습니다. 라자루스는 최근 AI 기술을 활용해 피싱 및 소프트웨어 공격의 속도와 정교함을 높이고 있으며, 국내 이용자를 대상으로 한 맞춤형 악성 문서 제작 등에도 AI를 악용하는 것으로 나타났습니다.

00abc760f5f261d17fa51df4.title_ko: 탈레스 CISO 세미나, AI 보안의 핵심으로 DSPM 강조
00abc760f5f261d17fa51df4.summary_ko: 탈레스는 AI 시대의 보안 전략으로 데이터 보안 태세 관리(DSPM)의 중요성을 강조했습니다. 생성형 AI 확산에 따라 비정형 데이터의 유출 및 권한 오남용 위험이 커지는 가운데, DSPM을 통해 데이터의 위치와 접근 권한을 지속적으로 파악하고 보호하는 거버넌스 체계 구축이 필수적이라고 설명했습니다.

1b20ffc8756856f7cf73e44d.title_ko: 네이버, 첫 오프라인 멤버십 행사 '넾페스타' 개최
1b20ffc8756856f7cf73e44d.summary_ko: 네이버가 멤버십 전용 오프라인 행사 '넾페스타'를 통해 쇼핑 및 결제 생태계를 오프라인으로 확장합니다. 행사장에는 안면인식 결제 서비스인 '페이스사인'과 NFT 기술을 결합하여 편리하고 안전한 관람 및 인증 환경을 구현했습니다. 이는 네이버가 자사 결제 기술의 오프라인 활용 범위를 넓히는 실험적인 시도로 평가됩니다.

271e55f19bd702f327dc23c3.title_ko: GS건설 자이 아파트 커뮤니티 시스템 해킹으로 입주민 개인정보 유출
271e55f19bd702f327dc23c3.summary_ko: GS건설 자이의 아파트 커뮤니티 예약 관리 시스템이 외부 비인가 접근을 받아 입주민 개인정보가 유출되었습니다. 유출 항목에는 이름, 연락처, 주소, 거주유형 등이 포함되었으며, GS건설은 한국인터넷진흥원 등에 신고하고 재발 방지 대책을 마련 중입니다.

d7ce1e6ddcc34000445da170.title_ko: 드루팔 커머스 코어 권한 우회 취약점 CVE-2026-118539 악용 발생
d7ce1e6ddcc34000445da170.summary_ko: 드루팔(Drupal)의 커머스 코어 모듈에서 인증 우회 취약점이 발견되어 실제 공격에 악용되고 있습니다. 해당 취약점은 2.41 이하 및 3.3.13 이하 버전에서 발생하며, 사용자는 즉시 최신 버전으로 업데이트해야 합니다.

88ff2696980ec98134784f07.title_ko: 미국 CISA, GitLab RCE 및 Cisco ASA 보안 취약점 KEV 목록 추가
88ff2696980ec98134784f07.summary_ko: 미국 사이버보안국(CISA)이 실제 공격에 활용되고 있는 GitLab RCE(CVE-2026-97229)와 Cisco ASA DoS(CVE-2026-76418) 취약점을 알려진 악용 취약점(KEV) 목록에 추가했습니다. 연방 기관들은 오는 11월 1일까지 해당 보안 패치를 적용할 것을 권고받았습니다.

a77db58d7b914f4cf3186d6e.title_ko: 시놀로지 NAS 기반 PHP 서비스에서 원격코드실행(RCE) 취약점 확인
a77db58d7b914f4cf3186d6e.summary_ko: 시놀로지(Synology) NAS의 PHP 기반 서비스에서 원격코드실행이 가능한 치명적인 보안 취약점이 발견되었습니다. KISA는 최신 NAS 운영체제 및 패키지 업데이트를 권고했으며, 특히 지원이 종료된 PHP 버전을 사용하는 경우 상위 버전으로의 전환이 필요합니다.

7f3465ece5177901a4ef952e.title_ko: 미국 빅테크 실적 충격 여파로 코스피·코스닥 급락
7f3465ece5177901a4ef952e.summary_ko: 미국 대형 기술주들이 AI 투자 부담과 실적 부진으로 약세를 보이면서 국내 코스피와 코스닥 지수가 3%대 하락했습니다. 특히 반도체 기업들에 대한 실적 우려가 커지며 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스 등 주요 기술주가 동반 하락했습니다.

b09d5bc0eb71c8268d14902c.title_ko: 레디스(Redis) 인메모리 DB 원격코드실행 취약점 5건 발견
b09d5bc0eb71c8268d14902c.summary_ko: 레디스에서 인증된 공격자가 메모리 오류를 악용해 서버를 장악할 수 있는 원격코드실행 취약점 5건이 발견되었습니다. 한국인터넷진흥원은 공식 수정 버전으로의 업데이트와 함께 외부 접근 제한 및 권한 최소화 등 보안 강화를 당부했습니다.

8cf28d4a33b96f3ebfc20532.title_ko: 라쿠텐 마리타임, 해사 산업 사이버 복원력 및 AI 신뢰성 논의 위한 'MATS 2026' 개최
8cf28d4a33b96f3ebfc20532.summary_ko: 라쿠텐 마리타임은 부산에서 국제 서밋 'MATS 2026'을 열고 해사 산업의 AI 도입과 사이버보안 대응 전략을 논의했다. 전문가들은 IACS 규제 준수를 넘어 선박 설계 단계부터 AI 신뢰성 검증과 가시성을 확보하는 실전적 사이버 복원력 강화가 필수적이라고 강조했다.

2516294ed7c28f804908a3e5.title_ko: 한국항공보안학회, '2026 항공보안포럼' 개최... AI 활용 보안장비 국산화 논의
2516294ed7c28f804908a3e5.summary_ko: 한국항공보안학회는 'K-항공보안장비 국산화 가속화 방안'을 주제로 포럼을 열고 인공지능과 정밀 센서를 적용한 보안장비 기술 자립을 논의했다. 산·학·연·관은 국산 보안 기술의 현장 보급과 독자적인 보안 인프라 경쟁력 확보를 위한 협력을 강화하기로 했다.

f27fd048dd55fadce6a5a7f8.title_ko: GS네오텍, AWS '에이전틱 AI 컴피턴시' 취득…엔터프라이즈 AI 보안 역량 입증
f27fd048dd55fadce6a5a7f8.summary_ko: GS네오텍이 아마존웹서비스(AWS)로부터 자율 추론 AI를 구현하는 '에이전틱 AI 컴피턴시'를 취득했다. GS네오텍은 AI 프로젝트의 보안, 데이터 거버넌스, 책임 있는 AI 설계 등 표준 프로세스 역량을 인정받아 향후 실무형 AI 에이전트 구축 서비스에 집중할 계획이다.

c253014ffe54a1045b3c56a4.title_ko: 중국 해커조직 '워프 판다', VMware 취약점 악용해 로그 기록 우회

CVE-2026-116241.description: pgAdmin 4's Import/Export Data tool wraps a user's query export in a psql \copy (...) TO command and checks that the query's parentheses are balanced so that nothing can escape the wrapper. The check rejected a backslash inside a single-quoted string, but not inside a double-quoted identifier, where it treated the next double quote as closing the identifier. psql's \copy parser applies the connection's escape character to whichever quote opened a token, so with standard_conforming_strings off a backslash-escaped double quote does not close the identifier. pgAdmin's and psql's view of the quoting then diverged, a closing parenthesis hidden from the check ended the \copy (...) wrapper, and a following TO PROGRAM clause was executed by psql on the pgAdmin host, as the operating-system account running pgAdmin, before the server rejected the statement. An ordinary database role can turn standard_conforming_strings off for itself, and the Import/Export Data permission is granted to non-administrators by default. This is a bypass of the fix for CVE-2026-17566. The fix rejects any backslash inside a double-quoted identifier, as was already done for single-quoted strings, since its meaning depends on a server setting that cannot be known reliably when the query is validated. This issue affects pgAdmin 4: before 9.19.
CVE-2026-116241.summary_ko: pgAdmin 4의 데이터 가져오기/내보내기 도구에서 따옴표 처리 방식 차이로 인한 우회 취약점이 확인되었습니다. 이로 인해 운영 체제 계정 권한으로 임의 명령이 실행될 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-119706.description: InternLM LMDeploy 0.9.0 through 0.18.0 contains an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability that allows remote attackers to run OS commands by sending pickled data to the /update_weights endpoint. Attackers can submit a base64-encoded crafted pickle in serialized_named_tensors, which ForkingPickler.loads deserializes without validation, executing commands as the api_server process.

CVE-2026-61738.description: SOCFortress CoPilot focuses on providing a single pane of glass for all your security operations needs. Prior to 0.1.77, `POST /api/scoutsuite/generate-gcp-report` in `backend/app/integrations/scoutsuite/routes/scoutsuite.py` admits admin and analyst users and validates the uploaded content as `GCPScoutSuiteJSON`, but passes raw `file.filename` from the multipart header to `save_file_to_directory` in `backend/app/integrations/scoutsuite/services/scoutsuite.py`. The writer combines this filename with `scoutsuite-report` using `os.path.join` without sanitization or a resolved-path containment check. A traversal filename therefore writes the supplied JSON outside the intended report directory. In the reported root-running backend, the researcher demonstrated root-owned writes outside that directory and into the application source directory. This permits host-file overwrite subject to the accepted JSON-content constraint and can disrupt application operation; the demonstrated primitive does not establish unrestricted executable contents or unconditional cross-tenant confidentiality loss. Version 0.1.77 removes caller-controlled filenames from the affected route; unrestricted-content and direct-code-execution claims require separate curator reconciliation.
CVE-2026-61738.summary_ko: SOCFortress CoPilot의 파일 업로드 처리 과정에서 경로 탐색 취약점이 존재합니다. 파일명을 검증하지 않아 공격자가 애플리케이션 외부 영역에 파일을 쓰거나 기존 파일을 덮어쓸 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: SOCFortress CoPilot의 경로 순회 취약점 등을 이용한 시스템 파일 덮어쓰기 및 관리자 권한 탈취

CVE-2026-119978.description: Flowise through 3.1.4 contains a sandbox escape vulnerability that allows authenticated users to execute OS commands by abusing allowlisted langchain and mammoth modules when ALLOW_BUILTIN_DEP=true. CVE-2026-119978.summary_ko: Flowise에서 샌드박스 탈출 취약점이 발견되었습니다. 인증된 사용자가 특정 모듈을 악용하여 OS 명령을 실행하거나 제한된 환경을 벗어나 시스템 접근이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-119116.summary_ko: AWS aws-nitro-enclaves-sdk-c의 kmstool-enclave 샘플 애플리케이션에서 Use-after-free 및 Double-free 문제가 발견되었습니다. 이로 인해 Nitro Enclave 내에서 힙 메모리 손상과 임의 코드 실행이 발생할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-90888.summary_ko: LeadSnap의 특정 버전에서 인증되지 않은 사용자가 PHP 객체를 주입할 수 있는 취약점이 보고되었습니다.

CVE-2026-116512.description: The Project Manager – AI Powered Project Management, Task Management, Kanban Board & Time Tracker plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 4.1.1 via the 'id' parameter parameter. This is due to unsanitized 'id' parameter value concatenated directly into the pipe-delimited validation rule string, which is then split and each token invoked as a dynamic PHP function with no allowlist check. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server. This is exploitable by unauthenticated attackers because WordPress core executes the route argument's validate_callback inside WP_REST_Server::dispatch() before the route's permission_callback is invoked, meaning the Project_Manage_Capability authorization gate is never reached on the vulnerable code path.
CVE-2026-116512.summary_ko: 워드프레스용 Project Manager 플러그인에서 id 파라미터 값 검증 미흡으로 원격 코드 실행 취약점이 발생합니다. 인증되지 않은 공격자가 서버에서 코드를 실행할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: 워드프레스 Project Manager 플러그인 내 인증 우회 및 원격 코드 실행 취약점

CVE-2026-119096.description: The Uncanny Toolkit for LearnDash plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in versions up to, and including, 3.8.2 via the `email` parameter of the `uo_login_action()` function. This is due to a parser-differential flaw in which the plugin's account-verification gate resolves the submitted `email` value using the raw, unsanitized string passed to `get_user_by()`, while the subsequent `wp_signon()` call relies on WordPress core's internal `sanitize_user()` to strip appended junk characters — causing the gate lookup to fail and be skipped entirely while the real account is still resolved and authenticated. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to log in to unverified or administrator-suspended accounts whose credentials they already possess, obtaining a valid `wordpress_logged_in` session cookie and defeating the plugin's account-approval and account-suspension controls. The nonce required to reach the handler is freely obtainable in the same request from the unauthenticated `ult-refresh-nonce` endpoint, making exploitation trivial for any attacker with network access to the site and knowledge of a target account's credentials.
CVE-2026-119096.summary_ko: Uncanny Toolkit for LearnDash 플러그인에서 인증 우회 취약점이 발견되었습니다. 파서 간 처리 방식의 차이를 이용해 인증되지 않은 공격자가 타인의 계정으로 로그인할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Uncanny Toolkit 플러그인 인증 우회로 관리자 계정 등 권한 탈취 가능

CVE-2026-104012.description: The Rox Appointment Booking – Appointment Booking Scheduling Solution plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation via Mass Assignment in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.1 This is due to the public `/rox-appointment-booking/v1/public/booking` REST endpoint performing mass-assignment of the raw request body into a new customer row while `CustomerModel::$fillable` includes the internal `wp_user_id` column, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to persist an arbitrary WordPress user ID alongside an attacker-controlled email address with no authorization check. When an administrator subsequently opens the poisoned customer record and clicks Update Customer, `SaveCustomer::handleRequest()` passes the stored `wp_user_id` and attacker-supplied email to `wp_update_user()` — succeeding because `LinkedAccount::canChange()` unconditionally returns true when the acting user holds the `edit_users` capability — thereby overwriting the targeted administrator's email address and enabling full account takeover via a standard WordPress password-reset request. Successful exploitation requires an administrator to open and save the poisoned record, and the attacker must know or guess a valid administrator user ID (such as the default user ID 1).
CVE-2026-104012.summary_ko: Rox Appointment Booking 플러그인의 대량 할당 취약점으로 인해 공격자가 임의의 사용자 ID를 주입할 수 있습니다. 관리자가 악성 레코드를 저장할 경우 관리자 계정 탈취가 가능합니다.

curation.reason_ko: Rox Appointment Booking 플러그인의 mass assignment 취약점을 통한 관리자 계정 탈취

CVE-2026-119086.description: Missing queue-set type validation in the queue-set selection system call in FreeRTOS-Kernel before V11.3.3 on MPU-enabled ports with queue sets enabled allows a local unprivileged task to write actor-controlled data beyond a pointer-sized object on the privileged kernel stack, affecting privileged memory across the MPU isolation boundary. To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to FreeRTOS-Kernel V11.3.3, rebuild, and reflash affected firmware. Builds that do not enable queue sets are not affected.
CVE-2026-119086.summary_ko: FreeRTOS 커널의 큐 세트 선택 시스템 호출에서 검증 부족으로 인해 커널 스택의 권한 있는 메모리가 덮어쓰여질 수 있습니다. MPU가 활성화된 환경에서 로컬 태스크가 권한을 격리하는 경계를 침범할 위험이 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: FreeRTOS 커널의 큐셋 시스템 콜 취약점으로 인한 권한 경계 침범

CVE-2026-61845.description: Crass is a Ruby CSS parser that's fully compliant with the CSS Syntax Level 3 specification. Prior to 1.0.7, Crass converts `CSS scientific notation` number values with unbounded exponentiation before clamping the result to `Float::MAX`. Applications that use Crass to parse attacker-controlled CSS strings can be forced to spend disproportionate CPU and memory parsing a tiny input, potentially resulting in a crash. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.7.
CVE-2026-61845.summary_ko: Crass 라이브러리가 CSS 수치 데이터를 처리할 때 지수 연산 제한을 수행하지 않아 과도한 CPU 및 메모리 자원을 소모합니다. 조작된 CSS 문자열을 파싱할 경우 서비스 거부(DoS) 및 프로그램 충돌이 발생할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Crass 라이브러리의 지수 연산 미제한으로 인한 CPU/메모리 고갈 DoS 취약점

CVE-2026-62162.description: Hydra is a layer-two scalability solution for Cardano. Prior to 2.1.0, the `Claim` branch in `hydra-plutus/validators/deposit.ak` checks only that `datum.head_id` matches the attacker-controlled `redeemer.currencySymbol` and that the transaction is valid before the deposit deadline. It neither requires spending the Head state-token UTxO in the same transaction nor constrains outputs. After a deposit made through `POST /commit` is confirmed, any third party able to build a Cardano transaction can observe and consume the pending deposit UTxO before its deadline and redirect the assets to an arbitrary address. A standalone deposit spend invokes no Head validator, bypassing its safety checks; historical head-ID binding and the Aiken rewrite retained this missing invariant. The default deadline is three times depositPeriod, so the described attack applies to pending deposits before that deadline. This issue is fixed in version 2.1.0.
CVE-2026-62162.summary_ko: Cardano용 Hydra 솔루션의 예치 검증 로직에 결함이 있어, 공격자가 예치금을 가로채 임의의 주소로 재지정할 수 있습니다. 검증 과정에서 예치 UTxO에 대한 보호 장치가 미흡한 점이 원인입니다.

curation.reason_ko: Hydra for Cardano의 예치 검증 결함으로 예치금 탈취 및 주소 재지정 가능

CVE-2026-63182.description: LightSAML implements SAML 2.0 data model classes, XML serialization and deserialization, XML security, certificate support, and message bindings. Prior to 4.7.1 and 5.0.1, LightSAML and xmlseclibs disagree about which assertion an inbound SAML signature covers. `Response::deserialize` uses `manyElementsFromXml` to collect only direct-child `saml:Assertion` elements of `samlp:Response`, and `AssertionSignatureValidatorAction` validates their `ds:Signature` using an out-of-band trusted IdP credential resolved by Issuer, not a key from the document. `XMLSecurityDSig::validateReference()` removes the enveloped signature from the shared DOM, but `processRefNode()` resolves `Reference URI="#id"` document-wide through an XPath of the form `//*[@Id]` and takes `item(0)`, which need not be the assertion whose claims LightSAML consumes. An attacker who has captured one genuinely signed assertion, such as an earlier login response, can place its signature-stripped bytes earlier in `samlp:Extensions` and present a forged direct-child assertion with the same ID and copied genuine signature. Validation then covers the hidden genuine bytes while LightSAML surfaces unsigned attacker-controlled `Subject/NameID`, `Conditions`, and `Attributes`, enabling authentication bypass or privilege escalation even when signature validation is required. The behavior was confirmed in versions 5.0.0 and 4.6.1. This issue is fixed in versions 4.7.1 and 5.0.1.
CVE-2026-63182.summary_ko: LightSAML에서 SAML 서명 검증 오류로 인해 인증 우회 및 권한 상승이 가능합니다. 공격자가 서명된 정보를 조작하여 신뢰할 수 없는 데이터가 정상적인 것처럼 처리되게 할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: LightSAML의 SAML 서명 검증 로직 결함으로 인한 인증 우회 가능

CVE-2026-104061.description: Scribus before 1.6.7 and 1.7.x before 1.7.4 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the scimgdataloader_psd loader that uses unchecked PSD file values as lookup array indexes. Attackers can convince users to place or import a crafted PSD file to corrupt heap memory, causing crashes and potentially code execution as the user.

curation.reason_ko: Scribus의 PSD 로더 힙 오버플로우로 인한 프로그램 충돌 및 코드 실행 위험

CVE-2026-119713.description: Paperclip 2026.403.0 before 2026.416.0 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows agent API key holders to set cleanupCommand and teardownCommand via PATCH /api/execution-workspaces/:id. When the workspace is archived, cleanupExecutionWorkspaceArtifacts runs these commands through a shell as the Paperclip server process, executing attacker-chosen OS commands on the server host.
CVE-2026-119713.summary_ko: Paperclip의 API 기능에서 공격자가 cleanupCommand 및 teardownCommand를 임의로 설정할 수 있는 원격 코드 실행 취약점이 발견되었습니다. 워크스페이스 아카이브 시 공격자가 지정한 명령이 서버에서 실행됩니다.

curation.reason_ko: Paperclip의 워크스페이스 정리 명령 조작을 통한 원격 코드 실행

CVE-2026-61620.description: HoneySQL turns Clojure data structures into SQL. From 2.0.0 until 2.7.1392, applications that pass user input or other arbitrary data into the HoneySQL `DSL` by calling `keyword` or `symbol` on that input can produce SQL strings that facilitate SQL injection when executed unchanged by a `JDBC` driver. Some formatters do not apply the existing suspicious-character check to the resulting entity names. The impact depends on the privileges of the database connection executing the generated statement. Input validation before constructing `keyword` or `symbol` entities is a workaround. The maintainer-designated fixed version is 2.7.1392.
CVE-2026-61620.summary_ko: HoneySQL 라이브러리에서 사용자 입력값을 키워드나 심볼로 변환할 때 발생하는 SQL 주입 취약점입니다. 적절한 검증 없이 데이터를 처리할 경우 데이터베이스에서 악의적인 쿼리가 실행될 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: HoneySQL의 SQL 인젝션 취약점으로 인한 DB 데이터 노출 및 변조 위험

CVE-2026-63341.description: Aedes is an MQTT broker that can run on any stream server. Prior to 1.1.1, the MQTT broker does not bound topic depth or structural complexity before passing topics through `mqemitter` into `qlobber`. A `PUBLISH`, `SUBSCRIBE`, or registered `Will` message containing an excessively deep topic can reach `qlobber._split_words` in `lib/qlobber.js` and trigger an uncaught `too many words` exception. Calls from `handlers/subscribe.js` and the publishing logic are not protected against that exception, so it escapes to the `Node.js event loop` and terminates the entire broker. The `Will` path is independently reachable when a client disconnects ungracefully: it calls `broker.publish` directly and bypasses the `PUBLISH` handler. An attacker must be able to establish an `MQTT session`, authenticated or unauthenticated according to broker configuration. A successful attack disconnects all legitimate clients and prevents reconnection until the broker process restarts. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.1.
CVE-2026-63341.summary_ko: Aedes MQTT 브로커에서 깊이가 과도한 토픽을 처리할 때 발생하는 예외 처리 미흡 취약점입니다. 이로 인해 브로커 프로세스가 종료되어 서비스 거부 상태가 발생할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Aedes MQTT 브로커의 예외 처리 미흡으로 인한 서비스 중단 DoS 취약점

CVE-2026-110023.description: The WP Data Access – App Builder for Tables, Forms, Dashboards, Charts & Maps plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 5.5.88 via the 'rel_tab' parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract every row and column of the underlying database table backing any anonymously published app, including WordPress user password hashes, email addresses, and password-reset keys from wp_users. Exploitation requires that an administrator has published at least one app with its REST API authorization set to 'anonymous', which is the standard configuration for publicly embedded apps.
CVE-2026-110023.summary_ko: WP Data Access 플러그인에서 rel_tab 파라미터를 통해 민감한 정보가 노출되는 취약점이 발견되었습니다. 익명으로 게시된 앱이 있는 경우 공격자가 데이터베이스의 모든 정보를 추출할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: WP Data Access의 데이터베이스 정보 노출 취약점으로 사용자 정보 탈취 가능

CVE-2026-119660.description: MuseBot before 2.0.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge admin sessions by using the hard-coded default session_key 'muse_bot_session_key'. Attackers can sign a MuseBot-session cookie carrying a user_id to gain full administrative access, reading password hashes, chat records, and bot configuration, and stopping bots.
CVE-2026-119660.summary_ko: MuseBot에서 하드코딩된 기본 세션 키를 사용하는 인증 우회 취약점이 발견되었습니다. 공격자는 이를 이용해 관리자 세션을 위조하고 전체 관리 권한을 획득할 수 있습니다.

522e832c3432537fcfecbd12.title_original: LRMoE: Demand-Side Load Re-Calibration for Efficient MoE Training on Memory-Constrained Nodes
522e832c3432537fcfecbd12.excerpt: arXiv:2610.37720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models offer scalable capacity for Web applications, but uneven routing creates computation and communication bottlenecks. Existing placement and replication methods redistribute this workload, yet additional expert copies compete with token-related buffers for limited GPU memory. We present LRMoE, a memory-aware MoE training system that jointly recalibrates backward demand and balances the retained workload. During forward execution, it plans retention quotas and expert placement under resource constraints while preserving all routed computations. During backpropagation, a load recalibration metric estimates each token-expert pair's contribution to the expert update and selects pairs within these quotas. A capacity-aware routing algorithm distributes retained pairs among eligible instances of their original experts. Physical compaction then forms smaller communication payloads and variable-size grouped GEMMs, reducing backward traffic, computation, and execution-buffer demand. Experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B and GLM4.5-106B-A12B show that LRMoE reduces cumulative MoE-layer training time to fixed-loss targets by 21.2-44.8% relative to SYMI.

798f98df6c3137e742f38a36.title_original: Amortized Localized Posterior Inference for Model Calibration with Application to an Ocean Turbulence Closure
798f98df6c3137e742f38a36.excerpt: arXiv:2610.37731v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model discrepancy may prevent a single calibration parameter from reproducing a physical response across the context domain. In addition, uncertainties in observations and contexts affect calibration and must be accounted for and quantified. We construct a family of localized posteriors by weighting observation likelihoods according to their proximity to a target context. Gaussian localization weights incorporate context uncertainty through covariance inflation, with reflection at domain boundaries and an optional correction for uneven context sampling. A conditional normalizing flow approximates the family of posteriors through amortized variational inference. Integrating the localized posteriors under a prescribed context measure gives the marginalized parameter distribution. In a twin experiment with the Branin-Hoo model, we compare global and localized inference under uniform and skewed context distributions. Localization reduces the reported aggregate predictive errors relative to the global posterior. An application to the k-$\epsilon$ turbulence closure in a single-column ocean model, with atmospheric surface forcing as context, shows that localized posterior calibration reduces temperature and zonal-velocity errors relative to deterministic and global-posterior calibration. Both twin experiments are constructed to admit local compensation.

4d043b925e277c305a81d3bb.title_original: ThinkJev: One Thought, Every Budget for Calibrated Typed Decisions
4d043b925e277c305a81d3bb.excerpt: arXiv:2610.37732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many uses of language models end in a typed decision: a choice among a closed set of options, whose probabilities code can act on. Reading those probabilities from one forward pass is fast but often wrong on decisions that take several steps, such as arithmetic, counting, and date comparison. Letting the model think first fixes most of these errors, but costs seconds per decision instead of milliseconds. To pay for thinking only where it helps, ThinkJev builds a fast and a slow system from one open hybrid-thinking model that can answer directly or after a thought. System 1 reads the model's probabilities for the option letters when it answers directly; System 2 reads the same letters after the model has thought on the same cached prompt, so escalating repeats no work and both systems give probabilities over the same options. Because the letters can be read after any number of thought tokens, one sampled thought also gives the answer under every thinking budget. Without training, ThinkJev lets System 1 answer alone only where a statistical test on labeled dev data guarantees that its accepted answers stay under a target error rate. At a 5% target, Qwen3.5-27B answers 24.5% of 8359 test decisions this way with a realized error of 3.9% (Qwen3.5-4B and 9B: 6.5% and 0.0%). For the rest, stopping each thought as soon as its answer is confident reaches 81.6% accuracy, against 82.7% for always thinking, with 72% of the thought tokens. C

c113c5f8f7f9f5385eb1f9b6.title_original: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
c113c5f8f7f9f5385eb1f9b6.excerpt: arXiv:2610.37739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown increasing promise in research-level problem solving, yet a comprehensive collection of such problems is still missing, and evaluating them on research-level problems remains challenging. We introduce OpenFrontiers, a cross-disciplinary resource that combines a structured corpus of open research problems with a retrospective benchmark of recently resolved problems in mathematics. The corpus records problem statements, context, progress, and other information for 12,151 problems. The benchmark contains 200 problems, 110 resolved in 2026 and 90 still open, each with a Lean~4 statement checked by automated probes and two independent reviews; a subset HQ-50 further filters based on quality score, etc. Our evaluation protocol grades formal proofs with two independent checkers in an isolated sandbox under closed-book, frozen-retrieval, and live-web conditions. Evaluating seven LLM agents on the HQ-50 subset under a standardized budget, we find that closed-book rediscovery is rare, at most 7 of 40 resolved problems, whereas live-web success mostly reflects retrieval of published solutions. By linking a broad research-problem corpus to a formally graded evaluation subset with documented solutions, OpenFrontiers provides a foundation for measuring research-level rediscovery and studying progress toward solving currently open scientific problems. 85c2602db1d7f1c3390dc82c.title_original: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments
85c2602db1d7f1c3390dc82c.excerpt: arXiv:2610.37786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web agents require diverse, executable, and resettable website environments for reproducible training and evaluation. Human-assisted mirrors demand per-site engineering, while generative construction can diverge from specified real websites. Capture-and-replay preserves observations, with interaction coverage constrained by captured content and replay capabilities. We present WebAnything, a fully automated framework that reconstructs source-grounded, reusable Web environments from real URLs without per-site manual implementation or repair after initial setup and authorization. An Explorer-Builder collects browser-observable structures, resources, and interaction outcomes; an independent verifier checks frozen candidates and guides local repair or targeted source recapture. We construct 244 website artifacts across 14 application domains and 53 categories, supporting 12,984 executed and accepted tasks. Compared with human-assisted WebHarbor, WebAnything achieves higher aggregate scores on three fidelity metrics, with 12 wins, two ties, and no losses in a blind audit. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B on 5,856 interaction trajectories improves REAL success by 9.9 percentage points, Odysseys-Easy Rubric Avg and Task Avg by 6.25 and 6.32 percentage points, and WebArena-Verified Overall success by 13.33 percentage points under the fixed harness. Code: https://github.com/china-qijizhifeng/Web-Anything

9f23406ca9231d6570bcdaa0.title_original: What Does an Ontology Catch? Curated, LLM-Generated and Data-Derived Ontologies as Checkers of LLM Agents over Knowledge Graphs
9f23406ca9231d6570bcdaa0.excerpt: arXiv:2610.37809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents that answer questions over Web knowledge graphs are increasingly wrapped in checks derived from the graph's ontology, on the assumption that a formal schema makes a reliable judge. Yet a checker can be wrong as well: it can miss errors, and it can flag correct answers and push the agent into "fixing" them. Whether a curated ontology is worth its cost as such a judge, and how it compares with an ontology an LLM writes or a schema mined from the data, is unknown. We make the checker itself the object of study. Across curated, LLM-generated and data-derived ontologies, used as prompt context, as a checker, or both, and across open-weight and proprietary agents on public graphs and a private graph of nearly $10^{9}$ triples, we account for what ontology-derived checks catch and what they wrongly flag. We show how each source trades caught errors against false alarms, how a curated schema used as published can contradict its own data, which errors structural checks miss, and whether combining sources or giving the agent the checker's specific feedback pays off. On UniProt, the curated ontology flags more correct answers than either an ontology derived from the data or one an LLM derives from a summary of the data with masked identifiers. On real agent answers, its flags are only marginally more precise than random flags.

bbc917e1ed164a48068bfaec.title_original: Measuring Where Intent Gets Lost in Agentic Smart Contract Synthesis
bbc917e1ed164a48068bfaec.excerpt: arXiv:2610.37830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents can now write software from a plain-English description, but code that runs is not the same as code that does what was asked. This gap matters most for smart contracts, the programs behind Web3 applications that move money on a blockchain and cannot be fixed once deployed. We ask how to check whether an AI-written contract behaves as it should, and where the requested behavior gets lost. We design an evaluation built on execution rather than opinion. We replay the same transactions on an AI-written contract and on the original it should reproduce and measure how often they agree. We test every grading tool on planted mistakes, compare against an answer key written without the description, and audit our own scorer until known wrong answers cannot pass. Common methods, such as AI judges and standard analysis tools, miss obvious mistakes, and scoring choices matter too. Checking only the functions every system includes hid about half the difference between pipelines. We then propose an elicitation-first architecture. Before writing code, the agent asks the client a short checklist of questions, checks the contract against an independently written executable answer key, and returns disagreements to the client instead of silently rewriting code. Asking first matters far more than reviewing or patching afterwards, across three AI models, while automated security fixes often break requested behavior. A few well-chosen questio

cfeaa173ceb8661e766e2cf8.title_original: Detecting Covert Collusion between AI Agents through Partner-Outsider Positive Listening
cfeaa173ceb8661e766e2cf8.excerpt: arXiv:2610.37849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents that share a secret convention can coordinate through messages that look innocent, so a monitor that reads only the messages can miss them. We propose a behavioural test: a partner that uses a code reacts to the exact wording of a message, whereas an uninvolved agent placed in its seat does not. Partner--Outsider Positive Listening (PoPLi) is the difference between the two agents in how much their action changes when the message is reworded with its meaning kept, and it is computed after the fact by replaying logged prompts. In a simulated market with five conditions (no collusion, a joint reward with neutral messages, the same with an openly stated intention, a covert first-letter code, and the code with a stated intention), PoPLi is between 0.48 and 0.59 whenever the code is present (95% intervals all above 0.29) and between -0.10 and -0.01 without it. Message-only monitors did not separate the conditions: one reading the speaker's messages answered "no" in all 50 markets, and one reading every seller's messages flagged 9 of 10 markets with no collusion. PoPLi detects the use of a private channel, not collusion as such, and it cannot detect collusion through incentives alone or codes carried by meaning.

aa75b4f7a32c2b8ae7455908.title_original: Evaluating and improving AI agents for sequencing protocol understanding
aa75b4f7a32c2b8ae7455908.excerpt: arXiv:2610.37851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing scientific-agent benchmarks rarely evaluate whether agents can reconstruct the exact molecular structures and generation workflows specified by sequencing protocols, a capability critical for analyzing customized sequencing assays. We introduce LibStructBench, a document-grounded benchmark for reconstructing sequencing-library structures and molecular workflows. Our experiments show that frontier agents often produce approximately correct reconstructions but remain unreliable at exact reconstruction, particularly in molecular-state representation and workflow connectivity. Switching the underlying language model produced larger average performance differences than switching agent harnesses, with a statistically significant difference only for molecular-state reconstruction. Additional knowledge improved oligo-family recovery in a small pilot without improving mean molecular-workflow scores. Autonomous accumulation of procedural rules and cross-protocol examples showed non-monotonic validation performance and no mean held-out molecular-workflow improvement in the tested trajectory. These findings highlight the need for more controlled and verifiable approaches to scientific reasoning about molecular processes in complex experimental protocols.

4b3273a5c9cfafc3552d99f7.title_original: Seq@K: Evaluating Language Models Under Sequential Feedback
4b3273a5c9cfafc3552d99f7.excerpt: arXiv:2610.37859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language-model agents differ fundamentally from prior intelligent systems in their ability to learn from natural language in context. This capability enables agents to iteratively refine their answers in response to feedback, a prevalent mode of operation in modern agentic workflows. However, the community primarily ranks models by metrics such as Pass@1 or Pass@K, which cannot capture how they utilize feedback on prior attempts. We introduce Seq@K, a natural evaluation protocol that measures whether a model can solve a problem within K sequential attempts, provided feedback after each previous failure. Unlike multi-turn agentic benchmarks that examine long-horizon planning, Seq@K isolates and formalizes the core capability of refinement from feedback. We evaluate Seq@K on a suite of 7 benchmarks and 16 frontier models, and show that Seq@K reveals a materially different model-selection landscape: under Seq@K, (1) model rankings often differ, (2) the Pareto frontiers admit more efficient configurations and (3) the gains from choosing the optimal model configuration can widen or shrink relative to those of Pass@K. We further show that analyzing model trajectories under Seq@K helps characterize iterative refinement behavior, such as the rate at which models address issues raised in feedback, or how rigidly they hold onto their own answers. 5682164ae0d1ece41cfa2976.title_original: What Constitutes Food Similarity? Visual Representations and Retrieval in Indian Cuisine
5682164ae0d1ece41cfa2976.excerpt: arXiv:2610.37867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Food similarity underlies retrieval, recommendation, substitution, and other food computing tasks, yet food representations are typically evaluated by identity preservation. We ask what happens to food similarity beyond identity: how different visual representations organize foods into relational neighborhoods, what culinary relationships these neighborhoods reveal or obscure, and how consistently these structures emerge across representations. Indian cuisine provides a challenging setting in which visually similar foods may have different culinary identities, while foods within a culinary family can vary substantially in appearance. Using an expanded Khana dataset and seven pretrained visual representations spanning convolutional, transformer-based, self-supervised, and image-text aligned models, we evaluate image-to-image retrieval and image-to-dish neighborhoods, examining culinary-family structure, contrast cases, and cross-representation agreement. We also aggregate image representations to compare dish-level visual similarity across models and against recipe-derived similarity for the same dishes. Image-level neighborhoods vary substantially across representations, including similarities across culinary-family boundaries. At the dish level, aggregation reveals common visual structure despite local variation, but this structure corresponds less strongly with recipe-derived similarity. cc918a1278e032632c79f7ee.title_original: Verification Learning Theory: A Process Model of Checking and Retention in AI-Assisted Judgment
cc918a1278e032632c79f7ee.excerpt: arXiv:2610.37875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate AI assistance can improve immediate judgments while reducing opportunities to practise the operations needed for independent performance. Verification Learning Theory (VLT) formalises this possibility for claim-evaluation practice followed by correct, independent, rule-specific feedback. The model links perceived assistant reliability to evidence checking and links the history of those checks to retained rule use. Its strict form assumes that task demands and perceived reliability influence learning only through checking, with equal learning per genuine check. It therefore predicts that perceived fallibility can improve delayed unaided judgment even without observed assistant errors, and that this advantage disappears when checking is already required and performed. Rule-specific gains and forecasts from checking histories provide further tests. Simulations examine the consequences and parameter dependence of these commitments; they do not constitute empirical validation. Comparisons with depth-of-processing and feedback-encoding accounts identify where predictions diverge and where the accounts remain observationally equivalent. The framework specifies experiments that can test the proposed mechanism and separates retention of practised rules from the broader problem of recognising which rule applies to a new claim.

49573aa590c1805f94941f87.title_original: The Anatomy of Socio-Demographics in Pluralistic Offensiveness Modeling: When and Where It Helps, and the Role of Reasoning
49573aa590c1805f94941f87.excerpt: arXiv:2610.37896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Subjective judgments such as offensiveness often vary substantially across individuals, motivating pluralistic modeling approaches that incorporate annotators' socio-demographic information to capture this variation. However, prior findings on the benefits of socio-demographic information for pluralistic modeling are mixed, calling for a systematic analysis of both its effectiveness and the mechanisms through which it improves prediction. In this work, we study $\textbf{when}$ and $\textbf{where}$ socio-demographics benefit pluralistic offensiveness modeling, as well as $\textbf{the role of explicit reasoning}$ in leveraging this information. Across three multi-annotator datasets with prompted and trained LLMs, we first show that demographic gains are small and inconsistent for individual predictions but become clearer at the group and population levels, because aggregation attenuates the idiosyncratic variation that masks small but systematic demographic signals. Second, using a reasoning and prediction format that explicitly decomposes individual judgment into an overall baseline and a demographic-specific deviation, we show that the gains arise from both components: demographic information improves baseline estimation and enables meaningful demographic-specific shifts, and interventions show that better component estimates improve final predictions. d556ac4d1e700c36d03d5b02.title_original: FilingLoop: Evaluating and Evolving LLM Agents for Corporate Disclosure Review and Revision
d556ac4d1e700c36d03d5b02.excerpt: arXiv:2610.37905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public disclosure repositories such as SEC EDGAR support informed investment through web access to corporate filings. Supporting their review with language model agents requires discovering unstated deficiencies across related documents, acquiring missing company facts, and verifying that requested revisions satisfy evidence-backed requirements. Existing financial question-answering evaluations provide limited evidence of these interactive capabilities. We introduce \textbf{FilingLoop}, an interactive benchmark and a self-evolving agent framework for corporate disclosure review and revision. Grounded in historical U.S.\ Securities and Exchange Commission correspondence, FilingLoop reconstructs 380 predominantly IPO review tasks from 96 companies under distinct information constraints. An evaluator separate from the acting agents scores final filings and responses against 6,099 eligible requirements and audits unsupported claims and harmful revisions. Our framework couples iterative review and revision within each case with procedural learning across cases, converting requirement-level evaluation feedback into role-specific guidance without updating model weights. Updates affect only subsequent cases, allowing procedural adaptation to be assessed without retrying scored tasks.
